content:
jordan_acme: Hey team — our customer is seeing 502s from /v1/generate in production starting ~08:12 UTC. Responses have no obvious request-id header and their proxy might be stripping headers. Can you list exactly what we should ask them to capture (minimal) and a curl they can run? They need step-by-step because their ops are not infra-savvy.

lina_support: Sorry you're stuck — we can get a repro quickly with a tiny set of artifacts. Minimal ask (in order):
1) exact UTC time window + example user/session id
2) raw response headers (copy/paste) or a single HAR of the failing request
3) an app log snippet showing the outbound request to our API (if available)
4) if the customer can run curl, one direct request to our regional endpoint so we can correlate server-side logs

lina_support: Quick curl they can paste and run (replace $KEY and payload):
```bash
curl -i -s -o /dev/null -D - \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-3p","input":"test"}' \
  https://api.redwood.inference/v1/generate
```
This prints response headers (look for `x-request-id` or `x-rw-trace`). If you see a 502 and no x-request-id, copy the full output and paste into the thread.

lina_support: If curl isn't possible, ask them to capture a HAR from the browser: DevTools -> Network -> reproduce -> right-click -> Save all as HAR with content. Attach the HAR to the ticket (redact user PII if needed).

jordan_acme: They said the API is behind an edge proxy and they can't get a curl directly. Any proxy-specific tips?

alex_oncall: If a proxy/CDN is in front, often headers are stripped or renamed. Two quick options:
- Ask ops to forward the request-id by adding the header `X-RW-Forwarded-Request-Id` from the edge to the backend.
- Alternatively, have them curl the regional backend host directly (bypass CDN): e.g. `https://us.api.redwood.inference/v1/generate` (region depends on customer).

alex_oncall: Also request they enable SDK debug logging for a brief window and capture logs. For our mobile SDKs set `RW_DEBUG=true` (Android: `adb logcat | grep redwood`), for JS set `localStorage.setItem('RW_DEBUG','true')` then reproduce and grab the console logs. Look for lines with `trace_id`, `request_id`, or `rw_trace`.

lina_support: If they can share a debug bundle from the Console that's ideal — it contains server-side correlation metadata. Steps: Console -> Support -> Create debug bundle -> copy the generated `debug_token` and paste here. That token lets us pull logs for the exact time window.

support-bot: Automated hint: when you supply a debug_token we'll try to correlate server logs and return up to 3 matching request_ids; please allow ~2–5 minutes for retrieval.

jordan_acme: Ops provided a small response dump but header names look different (`x-rw-id` not `x-request-id`). Is that enough?

lina_support: Yes, include that exact header name and value. We'll search all likely header names but please paste the header line exactly as shown. Example: `x-rw-id: 7a3f2d1b` — we can map that back. If you can, also paste the full response status line and body snippet.

alex_oncall: Final minimal checklist to give customer (copy/paste to them):
- Reproduce once with time window noted (UTC)
- Run the curl above and paste the full output (headers+status)
- If curl not possible: attach a HAR or browser network request (Save as HAR with content)
- Enable SDK debug for 60s and paste logs (look for `trace_id` / `request_id` / `rw_trace`)
- If behind proxy: either forward the RW header or curl direct to regional endpoint
- If available: generate a Console debug bundle and paste `debug_token` here

lina_support: If you post the curl output or debug_token I will run correlation and ping back with the server-side request_ids and the internal trace links. :thumbsup:

jordan_acme: Thanks — sharing curl output and the HAR now. I'll drop the debug_token when Console bundle is ready.
